the_split.statement: sum_{j=1}^k log(2 sin(j pi/N)) = k log(2pi/N) + log(k!) + sum_{j=1}^k logSinc(j pi/N), logSinc x = log sin x - log x
the_split.why: the j=0 singularity is SUBTRACTED, not estimated. The left side is singular termwise as j/N -> 0; the right side is a closed form plus a factorial plus a sum of a function continuous at 0

the_logsinc_sum_is_a_clean_euler_maclaur.claim: residual is O(h^3); residual . N^3 is flat in N

the_cancellation_that_needs_robbins.mechanism: Stirling contributes +1/(12k); logSinc'(x) = cot x - 1/x contributes -(h/12)(cot th - 1/th) = -(h/12)cot th + 1/(12k). The 1/(12k) pair cancels identically, leaving exactly -(pi/12N) cot th
the_cancellation_that_needs_robbins.consequence: the two halves are individually O(1/N) and only cancel together, so the refinement genuinely needs Robbins' 1/(12n) Stirling term — Mathlib's own docstring on le_log_factorial_stirling records that it is not formalised

the_precise_mathlib_gap.item_1: Euler-Maclaurin summation for a smooth function on a compact interval. Mathlib has Polynomial.bernoulli and sum_range_pow_eq_bernoulli but no summation formula
the_precise_mathlib_gap.item_2: the 1/(12n) term of Stirling (Robbins). Mathlib has le_log_factorial_stirling (effective, one-sided) and factorial_isEquivalent_stirling (asymptotic) only
the_precise_mathlib_gap.status: (A) is no longer blocked on a singularity; it is blocked on these two standard, clearly-named pieces
